title: Transport of monoidal unit replacement edges under a strong monoidal Quillen functor
statement:
Let $H:\mathcal M\to\mathcal N$ be an enriched strong monoidal left Quillen functor between closed symmetric monoidal differential graded model categories satisfying the model and enrichment axioms of [lem-coef-dg-model-mapping-comparison]. Left Quillen means that $H$ has an enriched right adjoint and preserves cofibrations and trivial cofibrations. The tensor has an enriched internal-Hom right adjoint in each variable, and its pushout product is a cofibration for cofibrations and trivial if either input is trivial. Assume the unit axiom in both categories: for a cofibrant replacement $t:U\to\mathbf1$, both $t\otimes K$ and $K\otimes t$ are weak equivalences for cofibrant $K$. Strong monoidal means that specified invertible tensor and unit comparisons satisfy the monoidal associativity and unit diagrams, and the symmetry diagram when $H$ is symmetric monoidal.

Let $q:Q\mathbf1_{\mathcal M}\to\mathbf1_{\mathcal M}$ be a cofibrant replacement. Suppose $v:H(Q\mathbf1_{\mathcal M})\xrightarrow{H(q)}H(\mathbf1_{\mathcal M})\cong\mathbf1_{\mathcal N}$ is a weak equivalence. Then for every cofibrant $K$ in $\mathcal N$ both composites
$$H(Q\mathbf1_{\mathcal M})\otimes K\xrightarrow{v\otimes1}\mathbf1_{\mathcal N}\otimes K\longrightarrow K,\qquad K\otimes H(Q\mathbf1_{\mathcal M})\xrightarrow{1\otimes v}K\otimes\mathbf1_{\mathcal N}\longrightarrow K$$
are weak equivalences, with final arrows the unitors. More generally form a finite nonempty tensor word in cofibrant objects of $\mathcal M$ and occurrences of $Q\mathbf1_{\mathcal M}$, and replace any subset of these occurrences by $\mathbf1_{\mathcal M}$ using $q$. Applying $H$ to this cube and using its strong monoidal comparisons identifies its edges with replacement by $v$ in the corresponding tensor words of $\mathcal N$. Every such edge is a weak equivalence. The edge maps commute with the specified associativity and unit diagrams of $H$ and of the two monoidal categories, and with symmetry diagrams when $H$ is symmetric monoidal.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, monoidal derived-unit condition: transport of unit-cube edges after applying a strong monoidal left Quillen functor. This is an agent-formulated foundation; no Stacks tag states the enhanced assertion.

proof.text: First record the tensor consequences of the stated axioms. A left adjoint preserves initial objects, so $H$ sends cofibrant objects to cofibrant objects. Since tensoring has a right adjoint, $0\otimes X$ and $X\otimes0$ are initial. The pushout product of $0\to K$ with $i$ is therefore $K\otimes i$ (or $i\otimes K$); for cofibrant $K$, both tensor functors preserve cofibrations and trivial cofibrations. Taking $i=0\to L$ also shows that $K\otimes L$ is cofibrant when $K,L$ are cofibrant. For a weak equivalence $f:X\to Y$ between cofibrant objects, apply [lem-coef-brown-split-factorizations] to obtain $pi=f$ and $ps=1_Y$, with $i,s$ cofibrations and $p$ a trivial fibration. Two-out-of-three makes $i,s$ trivial cofibrations. For either tensor functor $T$, $T(i),T(s)$ are weak equivalences; $T(p)T(s)=1$ makes $T(p)$ a weak equivalence, and $T(f)=T(p)T(i)$ is one too. This is a direct two-out-of-three deduction from the cited factorization statement, not an extra preservation assertion attributed to it.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, monoidal derived-unit condition: transport of unit-cube edges after applying a strong monoidal left Quillen functor.

proof.text: Put $A=H(Q\mathbf1_{\mathcal M})$ and choose a trivial fibration $q_{\mathcal N}:U\to\mathbf1_{\mathcal N}$ with $U$ cofibrant by factoring the initial map. Step 1 makes $A$ cofibrant. The lifting axiom applied to $0\to A$ and $q_{\mathcal N}$ gives $s:A\to U$ with $q_{\mathcal N}s=v$. Since $q_{\mathcal N}$ and $v$ are weak equivalences, so is $s$. Both ends of $s$ are cofibrant, so step 1 shows that $s\otimes K$ and $K\otimes s$ are weak equivalences for cofibrant $K$. The assumed target unit axiom gives the same for $q_{\mathcal N}\otimes K$ and $K\otimes q_{\mathcal N}$. If the axiom is read as given only for one cofibrant replacement $t:U'\to\mathbf1_{\mathcal N}$, lift $0\to U'$ against $q_{\mathcal N}$ to $u:U'\to U$ with $q_{\mathcal N}u=t$; $u$ is a weak equivalence between cofibrant objects by two-out-of-three, so $u\otimes K$ and $K\otimes u$ are weak equivalences by step 1, and two-out-of-three applied to $(q_{\mathcal N}\otimes K)(u\otimes K)=t\otimes K$ and its mirror gives the claim for $q_{\mathcal N}$. The composites $(q_{\mathcal N}\otimes K)(s\otimes K)$ and $(K\otimes q_{\mathcal N})(K\otimes s)$ are $v\otimes1_K$ and $1_K\otimes v$. Composing with the unit isomorphisms proves both displayed assertions. No cofibrancy of either monoidal unit is required.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, monoidal derived-unit condition: transport of unit-cube edges after applying a strong monoidal left Quillen functor.

proof.text: Fix any cube edge. Iterating the specified tensor comparisons identifies its image with a tensor word containing exactly one map $v:A\to\mathbf1_{\mathcal N}$ and identities on all other factors. Erase the other unit factors by the unitors, and reassociate the remaining factors on each side of this occurrence; the two resulting blocks $L,R$, when nonempty, are cofibrant by step 1. If both blocks occur, the edge becomes $1_L\otimes(v\otimes1_R)$. By step 2 the inner map is a weak equivalence between the cofibrant objects $A\otimes R$ and $\mathbf1_{\mathcal N}\otimes R\cong R$, so the tensor-preservation deduction from [lem-coef-brown-split-factorizations] in step 1 applies once more to $L\otimes-$. If exactly one block occurs, step 2 applies directly. If neither occurs, the edge is $v$, which is a weak equivalence by hypothesis. Conjugating by the associators and unitors preserves weak equivalences. This treats every partially replaced vertex, including a word consisting entirely of unit replacements, without treating an empty block as a cofibrant unit or permuting factors.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, monoidal derived-unit condition: transport of unit-cube edges after applying a strong monoidal left Quillen functor.

proof.text: The comparisons identify the actual edge maps, not just their endpoints: naturality of the binary tensor comparison gives $H(f\otimes g)$ as the conjugate of $H(f)\otimes H(g)$, and iteration gives the same identity for the finite word, with $H(q)$ followed by the unit comparison equal to $v$. For distinct replacement positions the two orders agree by the bifunctor identity $(f\otimes1)(1\otimes g)=f\otimes g=(1\otimes g)(f\otimes1)$, inserted in the word. Naturality of associators and unitors then makes every replacement square with a change of brackets or removal of a unit commute. The stipulated associativity and unit diagrams of the strong monoidal functor identify these squares before and after $H$. When $H$ is symmetric monoidal its stipulated symmetry diagram, together with naturality of the braiding, gives the same assertion for the symmetry faces. These are precisely the coherence diagrams required in the conclusion.
